# E11 — against RepoOMP on its NPB-C kernels

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** pre-flight

## The question

On identical programs and verification, are the agent's results verified correct at least as often as RepoOMP's released outputs? (H11)

## Result in one paragraph

Pre-flight (14 Oct, no model): of RepoOMP's eight NPB programs DiscoPoP profiles EP, IS and CG comfortably; LU needs two hours and 122 GiB of memory for one profile; on MG, BT and SP its explorer did not finish within two hours on one draw (repeats registered); on FT the explorer ends with the same error on every attempt (DiscoPoP candidate B26). As things stand the comparison can run on three programs — to be put to the author with the design.

## From the experiment record (§7 run log)

### `lulesh_ref_check`, `ref_check_mac`, `e11_npbc_probe_mac` — 2026-09-21, Mac, **the expert references through the harness** (no model)

**Question.** Do the expert versions the campaign measures itself against pass the harness's
own verification — LLNL's OpenMP LULESH, and hand-written references for the two dropped
benchmarks whose exclusion had not been verified (§5r)?

**How.** `agent/benchmark verify-source <bench> --source <reference> --threads 2,4 --repeats 3`;
LULESH at SMALL and STANDARD, the two kernels at their T0.1 verification size (LARGE).

| Reference | Verdict | Output | Speed (2 / 4 threads) |
|---|---|---|---|
| LLNL LULESH 2.0 OpenMP, SMALL | `parallel-not-faster` | dump 5.6e-15, seeded 4.2e-15, digest 1.8e-16 | 0.63× / 0.55× (8³ elements, 20 iterations) |
| LLNL LULESH 2.0 OpenMP, STANDARD | `FASTER` | the same | 1.31× / 1.70× |
| `hotspot`, chunk loop split | `FASTER` | byte-identical, shipped and seeded; digest error 0 | 1.44× / 1.52× |
| `floyd-warshall`, textbook form | `FASTER` | byte-identical, shipped and seeded; digest error 0 | 2.46× / 3.61× |

The FIRST LULESH run said `BROKEN` with a dump error of 0.25: a defect of the package, not of
LLNL's code (§6, same date) — corrected before the table above was taken. All four are Mac
numbers at no more than four threads: the speeds are indicative, and the correctness verdicts
must be repeated on the server at 6 / 12 / 24 threads before they are cited (`hotspot` is the
proof that four threads cannot see a schedule-dependent result).

**NPB-C probe (partial).** EP: instrument 1.9 s, run 10.0 s, explore 19.5 s, 6 do-all + 2
reduction patterns; IS: 1.8 / 0.7 / 18.8 s, 10 do-all; CG: 17.1 / 9.3 / 79.8 s, 24 + 9; NPB's
verification SUCCESSFUL in all three. FT had not finished instrumenting after 30 minutes when
the probe was stopped (the Mac was swapping, §6); FT, MG, BT, SP, LU are owed on the server.

| 2026-10-14 | result | **E11 pre-flight, the probe read out (`e11_npbc_probe_server`, server, no model): of RepoOMP's eight NPB programs DiscoPoP profiles three comfortably (EP, IS, CG), one in two hours with 122 GiB of memory (LU), three not within two hours (MG, BT, SP), and on one its explorer ends with the same error on every attempt (FT).** **Run:** `e11_npbc_probe_server` (valid), 13 Oct 22:14 UTC to 14 Oct 00:16 UTC at `90f9b35c4`, the DiscoPoP with B23 and B24 repaired; `tools/npbc_probe.py` at class S on RepoOMP's own inputs (the OpenMP sources with every pragma removed), each program with NPB's common units compiled as one unit, one process per program on four cores each, at most 7,200 s per step, the explorer run ONCE. Memory: `/usr/bin/time -v`'s maximum resident set size, its kilobytes over 1024² (GiB) — the largest single process, not a sum. NPB's own verification is successful in all eight instrumented runs. **Per program:** `EP` (170 lines, 2,506 call-path states): instrument 0.5 s, run 3.9 s, explorer 3.1 s, peak 0.2 GiB — Do-All 5, reduction 1; `IS` (663 lines, 638 call-path states): instrument 0.5 s, run 0.2 s, explorer 4.7 s, peak 0.2 GiB — Do-All 8, reduction 2; `CG` (469 lines, 47,667 call-path states): instrument 0.5 s, run 5.0 s, explorer 84.0 s, peak 5.3 GiB — Do-All 19, reduction 8; `FT` (703 lines, 13,444,805 call-path states): instrument 32.5 s, run 15.1 s, explorer 54.6 s, peak 16.5 GiB — the explorer ended with an error; `MG` (740 lines, 221,034 call-path states): instrument 1.0 s, run 0.6 s, explorer 7200.1 s, peak 2.5 GiB — the explorer was stopped at the limit; `BT` (2507 lines, 1,477,595 call-path states): instrument 4.8 s, run 10.5 s, explorer 7200.1 s, peak 14.2 GiB — the explorer was stopped at the limit; `SP` (2046 lines, 799,533 call-path states): instrument 2.7 s, run 3.4 s, explorer 7200.3 s, peak 9.5 GiB — the explorer was stopped at the limit; `LU` (2599 lines, 84,429,621 call-path states): instrument 178.4 s, run 49.0 s, explorer 7075.5 s, peak 122.5 GiB — Do-All 147, reduction 43. **Read against the scope rule** (D26, 20 Sep: a program DiscoPoP cannot profile within two hours is out; measured once and reported). *In:* EP, IS, CG — one profile in 7 s, 5 s and 89 s. *LU:* the profile completes, with 147 Do-All loops and 43 reductions, but its explorer needs 7,076 s — two minutes under the limit — and 122 GiB. The agent as built gives the explorer 600 s per attempt and five such attempts (`EXPLORER_STALL_S`, `EXPLORER_STALL_ATTEMPTS` in `profiling/tools.py`): under its defaults LU's profile fails after 50 minutes; with `--explorer-timeout` raised, every profile — the first and the one after each rewrite the agent keeps — costs two hours, against the harness's limit of 90 minutes per phase of a trial. So no trial can run on LU: reported as profiled, out of the trials. *MG, BT, SP:* the explorer was stopped at two hours — MG's and SP's logs end in warnings about tasks, BT's in a pass over source locations that stood at 21 % after nine minutes — on ONE draw each. The explorer is known to stall on one draw and finish on the next (L5), so one draw does not say which this is: three more attempts each on the kept profiles, with the agent's limit of 600 s, are registered as `e11_npbc_explorer_repeats` and run next; until then the three are *not profiled within the limit on one draw*. *FT:* the explorer raises `ValueError: Invalid iteration structure found at node: Start IT 5:612` in `TaskGraph.__assign_loop_contexts` after 55 s. Repeated at once on the kept profile (`e11_npbc_explorer_repeats`, part `FT`, 14 Oct 00:27–00:30 UTC, three attempts, the explorer's output moved aside between them): the same error at the same node after 53 s in 3 of 3 — with the probe's draw 4 of 4. So it is not a draw: the agent's twenty attempts would all end there, and FT cannot be profiled with this DiscoPoP. The symptom is B2's (repaired in September for loops with several back edges); line 612 of `ft.c` lies in the condition before the first of `verify`'s five loops, each of which leaves through two `break`s — not traced, no reproducer yet. Listed as the candidate **B26** in `discopop_agent/docs/DISCOPOP_BUG_REPORTS.md`; whether it is repaired — a change of the DiscoPoP every later run uses — is the author's decision, as with B23 and B24. **Against the Mac probe of 21 Sep** (`e11_npbc_probe_mac`, September's DiscoPoP, class S): EP, IS, CG profiled there too, with 6 + 2, 10 + 0 and 24 + 9 Do-All + reduction patterns; here 5 + 1, 8 + 2 and 19 + 8. Another DiscoPoP (the repairs of 26 Sep to 12 Oct, B8 to B24, lie between) on another machine; which repair moved which count was not examined. **What it means, to be put to the author with E11's design:** the comparison "on RepoOMP's eight kernels" can run on three of them as things stand; MG, BT and SP depend on the repeats, FT on a repair, LU is out by cost. **For the fast refresh's benchmark:** the candidates among these are EP, IS and CG; at class S their instrumented runs take 3.9, 0.2 and 5.0 s — far below the minute the rule asks for; the next two classes are screened next. **Left on the server, not in the archive:** the profiles of FT (7.3 GB on disk), BT, SP and MG (1.6 GB together), kept for the repeats and for the look at FT. |
| 2026-10-13 | result | **E6 pre-flight, the smoke (`e6_lulesh_smoke`, server, no model): the September package of LULESH cannot be profiled through the run path — its header has no include guard, and the profile step compiles the six units as one. A defect of my package of 21 Sep, found by the first trial it ever went through; nothing of DiscoPoP's or of LLNL's.** **Two launches — a deviation from the plan row's command.** The first (22:14 UTC, at `90f9b35c4`) was refused by the runner before a run existed: `llnl/lulesh` has no entry in `kernel_sizes.json` (T0.1 is owed, as the plan row says), and the run path wants a verification size. Launched again at 22:16 with `--verify-size STANDARD` — the size at which LLNL's own version was FASTER on the Mac; nothing else changed. Each launch made the launcher's one auth-check call; no trial called a model. **What came.** One trial, `PROFILE_ERROR` after 0.31 s of the instrumenting step: 20 compile errors (the compiler's limit), every one a redefinition out of `lulesh.h` (`VolumeError`, `SQRT`, `Domain`, `cmdLineOpts`, …) with the compiler's note "unguarded header". For a program of more than one file the profile step writes a unit that includes every unit (`dp_harness_unity.cpp`, D6 — DiscoPoP needs the whole program in one unit to keep its loop states), so `lulesh.h`, which each of LULESH's units includes, arrives several times; it carries no include guard — in the package and in LLNL's sources alike, where the units are compiled one by one and none is needed. The reference check of 21 Sep (`lulesh_ref_check`) verified the package without profiling it, so it could not see this. **Shown on the Mac, compile only** (the six units of the package as one unit, `clang++ -fsyntax-only`): the same 20 errors; with `#pragma once` as the header's first line, none. **Not shown:** that the instrumented build, the profiled run and the explorer then go through on the repaired DiscoPoP (the August profile took 28 GB) — that is the next smoke, with the package repaired through its generator and checked again against the original's report at three sizes. It waits for the NPB probe to end: the server's copy is not synchronised during a run. **The NPB probe** (`e11_npbc_probe_server`) was started at 22:14 UTC at `90f9b35c4`, eight processes on cores 12 to 43; EP and IS ended within a minute (both profiled, NPB's own verification successful); the other six were running when this row was written. **What it means for the plan:** step 2 for LULESH starts with a repaired package; the guard is one more change of ours to a file a model would read, and goes into the proposal of the packages' form. |

The author's rule of 4 Oct — the file the model reads is an ordinary code file, no harness, no notes of ours — was built for TSVC's one-function files; what it means for a program whose computation shares a file with `main` is proposed to him with the texts a model would read, before any model call. **Footprint.** 7.1 GB per LULESH profile at the smallest size (the run path keeps no profile tree in the archive); the server has 387 GB free. **What is already decided for these experiments** (13 Oct): the agent's entry is the setup in which the model writes the pragma; E11's row of 21 Sep pre-stated both setups side by side, and both stay there. **Registry:** group E6 registered (pre-flight); the two runs registered before launch. |
